extra_computation_detail: The descriptive window summaries and candidate-setting prediction are useful. Welch is a defensible alternative to a pooled-variance test; unequal variances do not require stopping all comparisons. Brown–Forsythe and Mann–Whitney provide supplementary evidence but do not resolve serial dependence or temporal confounding. Calculating window Ppk is permissible descriptively, but using its modest point-estimate increase to assert capability improvement is not justified without resolving the moving-range signal and addressing estimation uncertainty. The selected reduced-model prediction is suitable for planning confirmation, not a validated optimum or a selection-adjusted guarantee.
